title: Character theming and portrait coherence
problem: No plan covers the characters' look and theme as a whole. PLAN-027 and PLAN-033 handle the palette, sizes and screens; the naming plan handles words. Nobody owns: one portrait style for animals and humans, the costume and theme rules for customers, quirks and titles that follow the cast rules, a diversity pass over the 36 customers, and the same art on the screen, the printed cards and the gallery.
scope: Update the creative bible (cast and portrait rules) for Look C and board look D: portrait grid, face template, outline, light direction, palette roles for skin, hair and costume
Customer theme rules: costume archetypes, a title and quirk pattern ("what they do, not who they are"), a diversity pass over all 36 customers and the three event customers
Shopkeepers stay animals (DEC-018); bring animals and humans to the same outline, light and palette rules
An audit sheet of every portrait against the rules, with a list of fixes the owner approves
Apply the fixes; the screen, the printed cards, the character pick and the gallery all draw from the same data
Optional, owner decides: idle, happy and sad frames for the shopkeepers
exclusions: Changing any perk, order or rule
New customers beyond replacements the owner asks for

acceptance.text: The creative bible has the portrait and theme rules and the owner approves them
An audit sheet lists every portrait against the rules and the owner approves the fix list
The approved fixes are applied and the screen, printed cards, character pick and gallery show the same portraits
Every customer title and quirk follows the cast rules (a check lists any that name who someone is)
Phone look checked on the character pick, the table and the results screen
Lint, types, unit tests, build and browser tests pass
